title: Apostolic and Disciple Writings — Unified Historical Collection
ordering: Historical events and settings represented by the apostolic- and disciple-associated writings control the order, never composition dates. The Greek/Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter is immediately before Revelation. Revelation is the final record. The Coptic Apocalypse of Peter is a separate work, placed by its own narrative setting.
scope: All identifiable writings connected by historical attribution, claim, tradition, subject, or early community use to apostles and disciples, including gospels, letters, testimony, acts, instruction, apocalypses, and other related writings. Inclusion is not an endorsement of authenticity, apostolic authorship, inspiration, or historical accuracy.
anti_compilation_rule: Do not use the later 27-writing compilation as the archive boundary or as the ordering template. Preserve its history as one later classification only.
date_policy: Composition date estimates are stored separately from physical witness dates. Use null for undetermined dates; never use numeric sentinels. Where estimates overlap or are disputed, show a date band and mark sequence as approximate.
evidence_policy: Every entry must distinguish title tradition, actual author identification, date of composition, earliest surviving witness, manuscript text status, and historical reliability. Anonymous or pseudonymous works must not be presented as verified apostolic authorship. New additions include scholarly research-source URLs. A source supports only the claims described in its entry; it does not automatically verify every textual or attribution statement.

records.historical_anchor: John's Patmos setting and messages to seven assemblies in Roman Asia
records.historical_anchor_basis: Revelation 1:4 identifies seven assemblies in the province of Asia; 1:9 places John on Patmos because of the word of God and the witness of Jesus; 1:11 names the seven destinations. Chapters 2–3 address those assemblies, while 22:16 again frames the work as testimony for the assemblies. The text does not identify John as the son of Zebedee, so that identification must remain separate from the stated name. The date is disputed: a late-first-century setting, often associated with Domitian, is widely argued, while some scholarship proposes a date around 68–69 CE under Nero. The language of suffering does not by itself prove an empire-wide official persecution; local pressures and conflicts are also considered. Patmos is the stated location of John's vision, but whether every stage of composition occurred there is not certain.
records.historical_order_note: Final record in the collection by explicit archive arrangement. Its Patmos setting and disputed date remain separate; final placement is not a claim about the chronological fulfilment of every vision.

historical_chronology_policy: Use the events and historical setting represented in each writing as the organizing basis. For narratives, follow narrated events. For letters and instruction writings, use the historical situation, people, journeys, imprisonment, or community events they address. If an exact setting cannot be established, use a broad labelled period and mark placement provisional. Never use composition date as a substitute for event chronology. Revelation is the final catalogue record by explicit archive arrangement; the Greek/Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter is immediately before it. The Coptic Apocalypse of Peter is a separate work placed by its own Jerusalem-before-crucifixion narrative setting.

chronology_policy.primary_rule: Use events narrated or historical situations addressed, not composition or manuscript dates.
chronology_policy.overlapping_narratives: Group accounts covering the same events rather than claiming an unsupported order among them.
chronology_policy.letters: Use internal references, journeys, communities, conflicts and imprisonment settings; mark disputed reconstructions.
chronology_policy.later_accounts: Identify later retellings as later narrative claims, not verified eyewitness chronology.
chronology_policy.uncertainty: An unresolved historical anchor must remain provisional; do not invent exact dates.
chronology_policy.subsequence: The records array is physically ordered by historical_sequence, then historical_subsequence. Equal values mean no exact relative order is asserted; title order is only a neutral display tie-breaker and never uses composition date.
chronology_policy.non_narrative: Sayings collections, sermons and writings without a single event sequence are explicitly identified as not internally chronologically placeable.
chronology_policy.later_claims: Later pseudonymous narratives are placed by the scene they claim to narrate only where a scene is identifiable; this does not authenticate the event.
chronology_policy.unplaced_group: Writings without a sufficiently secure event sequence are shown in a separate final group. This group is not ordered by composition date.

scope_policy.inclusion: This unified catalogue is limited to writings attributed to, associated with, or reporting correspondence of apostles and early disciples, including later works written under their names. Inclusion does not prove authorship. Include fragmentary, lost, hypothetical, pseudonymous, and later writings where an apostolic/disciple connection is claimed or studied, while labelling the strength of evidence. Inclusion does not prove authenticity.
